question: A woman goes to the emergency room three days after being subjected to extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy on a calculation of 2.1 cm maximum diameter located in the left kidney. He presented poor general condition, pain in the left renal fossa, nausea and fever of 39.2ºC. Simple Rx is performed in which several small calculi are seen in the area of ​​the left distal ureter. The radiologist informs us that on ultrasound he observes the existence of left pyelocalicial grade II dilatation. The next step should be:

options.opa: Urinary ureteroscopy given the existence of obstructive uropathy of lithiasic cause.
options.opb: Income with intravenous hydration, as well as antibiotic treatment, given the suspicion of urinary infection.
options.opc: Urgent urinary diversion (ureteral catheterization or percutaneous nephrostomy) given the suspicion of complicated obstructive uropathy.
options.opd: New session of extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy, previous symptomatic treatment of the patient with anti-inflammatory, antibiotic treatment and intravenous hydration.
